findings.message: U106 (TPS70950DBVR): V(EN-GND) 6.5 vs rating 7 (93%) (ch1/CH1_V5EN to TAP0) — above 80% derating
findings.waived_by: designer: EN is left floating with only C(k)39 to GND, which SBVS186H Table 5-1 allows ('can be left floating to enable'; must stay below 6.5 V). The self-biased level of the internal 300 nA pull-up is not published, so the net envelope is the 6.5 V recommended maximum (93 % of the 7 V absolute maximum); nothing drives EN higher.

findings.message: RT101 (470k NTC): voltage 5.05 vs rating 5 (101%) between ch1/CH1_TH and TAP0 — exceeds rating
findings.waived_by: designer: NCP15 'maximum voltage' 5.00 V is Murata's self-heating limit (spec note *4). The NTC sees 5.05 V only when cold (R_NTC >= 6 MOhm below -20 C), where it dissipates < 5 uW (< 0.002 K self-heating); at the 95 C trip it has 2.5 V and 0.25 mW.

findings.waived_by: designer: Hydrogen ignition is controlled by where the enclosure is installed (outside the battery box, not above vents) and by having no relays or user-operated contacts on the board; installation rule in DESIGN.md 9.

findings.message: Q-1 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Confirm N = 2-4. Is a > 4-battery (96 V) bank needed? A > 70 V stack is outside this safety analysis.

Q-2 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Battery model and charger set-points (float, absorb, equalize, temperature compensation)? The wake threshold is 13.23 +/- 0.09 V per battery (R120-R125); a float below ~13.3 V may never wake the balancer.

Q-4 is BLOCKING and unanswered: MLCCs and an electrolytic sit directly across each battery. If one shorts, the on-board fuse clears. Acceptable, or must they be series-redundant pairs (+16 caps per channel, +8 mm board)?
Q-12 is BLOCKING and unanswered: Certification target (UL 1973 / IEC 62368-1)? If yes, re-derive spacing from purchased standards.
